content:
The Mexican government is taking the death of 56-year-old Emiliano Andrade Covarrubias to the courts and to Washington. According to a report published October 23, Mexico is filing a formal legal complaint through the Webb County district attorney and the U.S. State Department following Andrade Covarrubias’s death at the Rio Grande Processing Center in Laredo.

Andrade Covarrubias, a Mexican national who had been detained since June 2026, was found unresponsive at the facility on October 17. Mexican authorities say he suffered from diabetes and high blood pressure. Mexico’s foreign ministry reports that 18 Mexican nationals have died in ICE custody or during immigration operations since January 20, 2025.

President Claudia Sheinbaum publicly addressed the case at an October 19 press conference, and Mexico’s foreign minister contacted the family on October 18, according to the report. Mexico’s Consulate General has asked U.S. authorities for a detailed account of the circumstances surrounding the death.

What is disputed — and what is verified

Webb Watch has followed this case since October 20, when conflicting accounts emerged over the medical care Andrade Covarrubias received in detention. The precise circumstances of his death remain under investigation, and ICE’s account of events differs from the concerns raised by Mexican officials. This story reports what the Mexican government says it is doing — filing a legal complaint and diplomatic notes — not a finding about what happened at the facility.

What is verified: a 56-year-old Mexican national died October 17 at a federal immigration processing center in Laredo; Mexico is pursuing formal legal and diplomatic channels, including the Webb County district attorney’s office; and the consulate has requested a full accounting from U.S. authorities. Any conclusion about responsibility will have to wait for the investigations Mexico, Webb County, and federal authorities are conducting.

Why it matters for Laredo

This is no longer just a federal immigration matter. By routing its complaint through the Webb County district attorney, Mexico has made the case a local legal matter too — which means Laredo will be watching how the county’s own justice system handles a request from a foreign government tied to a death at a federal facility inside Webb County. Diplomatic cases like this also put a spotlight on medical standards in detention facilities nationwide.

title: Mexico Files Formal Legal Complaint Over Death of Emiliano Andrade Covarrubias at Laredo ICE Facility
